page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.large is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and does not include GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Supported CPU instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Benchmark testing indicates moderate performance in single-threaded workloads compared to multi-threaded execution. The instance achieves a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 24.5 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 1281.0. Multi-threaded benchmark scores reflect the single physical core architecture, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1600.0 and a passmark CPU score of 2713.74. Memory throughput tests recorded uncached read speeds of 22.35 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 14.76 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput reached 1.73 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 2.05 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers a small footprint with dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding CPU credit depletion risks associated with burstable instances. However, resource limits constraint high-concurrency throughput. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.large provides optimal resource density for lightweight microservices, small web servers, basic background worker processes, and single-threaded batch tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.large is an entry-level compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Built on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, it offers 2 vCPUs spanning a single physical core, 4.0 GB of memory, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, but lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Hardware acceleration supports AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instructions. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core efficiency, reaching a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 24.5 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 1281.0. However, multi-threaded performance and memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the dual-thread single-core hardware profile, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1600.0. The server provides a cost-effective choice for light background processes, small web microservices, and single-threaded tasks.
